footerNote: Coinbase reports no gross-profit line; 'Transaction expense' — the direct cost of processing trades — is shown as cost of revenue. Coinbase also reports two gain lines inside operating expenses (a $0.1M gain on crypto held for operations and $8.6M of other operating income — $9M in total); the chart shows that $9M in the 'other income' step instead, so the chart's operating profit is $161M rather than the reported $170M — net income is unchanged. Figures are from Coinbase's Q3 2024 shareholder letter (Exhibit 99.1) and Form 10-Q.

segments.name: Transaction revenue
segments.note: Fees from crypto trading — consumer $483M, institutional $55M, other $34M. Trading volume was $185B, down 18% from Q2 as volatility eased, but revenue nearly doubled from a year ago.

segments.name: Subscription and services
segments.note: Steadier income: stablecoin revenue $247M, blockchain rewards $155M, interest and finance fees $64M, custodial fees $32M, and other services $59M.

takeaways.text: Transaction revenue rose 98% year over year to $573M — consumer trading alone was $483M — even though volume fell 18% from Q2 to $185B as crypto volatility eased.
takeaways.title: Trading nearly doubled from a year ago

takeaways.text: Subscription and services revenue rose 66% year over year to $556M, almost as much as trading brought in — stablecoin revenue was the biggest piece at $247M, ahead of blockchain rewards at $155M.
takeaways.title: Steadier revenue nearly matched trading

takeaways.text: A $121M pre-tax loss on crypto Coinbase holds as an investment — mostly unrealized, $92M after tax — held net income to $75M, even though Adjusted EBITDA was $449M for a 7th straight positive quarter.
takeaways.title: Paper crypto losses capped profit

verdict: Coinbase's revenue rose 79% from a year ago to $1.21B as trading revenue nearly doubled, but a $121M paper loss on the crypto it holds as an investment held net income to $75M.
